# Vehicles

**Generated** from `vehicles/*.json` by `tools/vehicles/build.py`. Do not edit this file — edit the car and rerun.

---

## The deck does not change. Only the adapters do.

Every car below takes the same deck: the same ESP32, the same panel, the same DAC, mux, tuner and firmware, built to the one shopping list in [BUILD.md](BUILD.md). It fits an **ISO 7736** aperture and speaks **ISO 10487**, and those two standards are the entire reason a home-built head unit drops into anything.

What varies is a bag of adapters — something to fill the hole, something to reach the car's connector, something to reach its aerial — and how much room is behind the dash.

> ### The one people get backwards
>
> **The radio region follows where you drive, not where the car was built.** A JDM import in Britain receives British stations, so it wants the European band plan. Everything *else* about fitting an import follows the car's market.
>
> It is not a subtle failure. Japan's FM band is 76–95 MHz against Europe's 87.5–108, so a European deck driven in Japan can tune about a tenth of the band. The Americas use 10 kHz AM spacing against 9 kHz elsewhere, and on the wrong step every station lands between channels. The deck stores the region in NVS and it is set once — see `deck_tuner_region_set()`.

## Confidence

| | Means |
|---|---|
| ✅ | Checked against a datasheet, a standard, or a fact not in dispute |
| ⚠️ | Believed true and **not confirmed** — check before buying |
| 📏 | Varies car to car. Measure yours; do not trust any list, including this one |

**There are no retailer part numbers here on purpose.** They change, they are regional, they go out of stock, and a stale one looks authoritative. What you get is the thing to search for, which does not go stale.

## Honda S2000 AP1

**1999–2003** · also known as AP1 2.0 F20C · markets: UK, EU, US, JP, AU

<sub>`vehicles/honda/s2000/ap1.json`</sub>

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| **Does the deck fit** | ⚠️ yes — the deck goes in as built | The dash takes a single-DIN unit in a surround. Nothing about the deck needs changing; it is the standard 182 × 53 mm face. |
| **Aperture** | ⚠️ single DIN (ISO 7736), one slot | Confirm against your own car before ordering a fascia — the surround differs between the early and late dash. |
| **Depth behind the dash** | 📏 tight. The S2000 centre stack is shallow and sits against the transmission tunnel | This is the number that decides whether the build fits, and it is the one no listing tells you. Measure from the back of the aperture to the nearest obstruction before you commit to a chassis depth. |
| **Fascia** | ⚠️ search: “Honda S2000 single DIN fascia adapter” | Only needed if you are not reusing the car's own surround. Reusing it looks far better and costs nothing. |
| **Harness adapter** | ⚠️ search: “Honda 20-pin to ISO 10487 harness adapter” | Honda used their own multi-pin connector, not a bare ISO block. The adapter is the standard fit-any-aftermarket-radio part and is cheap and widely stocked. |
| **Aerial adapter** | ⚠️ search: “Honda aerial adapter to DIN (Motorola)” | Check whether your car's aerial is powered. If it is, the deck has no aerial-power output — see the gotcha below. |
| **Steering-wheel controls** | ✅ none — no factory steering-wheel audio controls, any generation, any market, any trim | The S2000 has no steering-wheel controls at all — not audio, not cruise. This is the single biggest simplification of the whole build for this car: no interface box to buy, no wire to run to the column, and no learning step during bring-up. |
| **Dash dimmer** | ⚠️ dash dimmer available at the ISO A connector | Standard ISO A6. Meter it — ISO fixes the connector, not the pinout. |
| **Switched live** | ⚠️ switched live available at the ISO A connector | Standard ISO A7. Commonly swapped with A4 permanent live by manufacturers; meter before connecting. |

**Same as the other generations**

- No steering-wheel controls, so no SWC interface and no learning step
- Single-DIN aperture, so the same deck and the same fascia strategy
- Same Honda harness family, so the same adapter search term

**Differs from the AP2**

- Nothing that affects this build has been identified. AP1 and AP2 differ in engine, gearbox ratios, suspension and — from 2004 — the instrument cluster, none of which touch the head-unit aperture, the harness or the aerial.

**By market**

- UK / EU / US / AU / JP cars are believed to share the head-unit aperture and harness family. The differences between them are LHD/RHD, the cluster and the badge, none of which reach the centre stack.
- ⚠️ The one thing that DOES differ is the radio band plan, and it follows where the car is now, not where it was built. A JDM AP1 in Britain wants the UK plan.

**Gotchas**

- Depth, not width. Measure the space behind the aperture before building the chassis — the S2000's centre stack is shallow and this build is ~160 mm plus another 30–40 mm for plugs.
- The deck has no aerial-power output. If the car has a powered or amplified aerial, it needs its 12 V from a switched source of your own; the deck will not supply it.
- The deck is line-out only and has no amplifier. The S2000's speakers expect to be driven — plan for an amplifier, or accept that it will be quiet.
- It is a convertible. Water gets into a centre stack far more readily than in a coupé; think about where the boards sit before the first wet week.

## Mazda MX-5 NA

**1989–1997** · also known as Miata (US), Eunos Roadster (JP) · markets: UK, EU, US, JP, AU

<sub>`vehicles/mazda/mx-5/na.json`</sub>

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| **Does the deck fit** | ⚠️ yes — the deck goes in as built | Single-DIN dash. The oldest and simplest case in this directory. |
| **Aperture** | ⚠️ single DIN (ISO 7736) | Confirm on your own car; the console was revised during the run. |
| **Depth behind the dash** | 📏 shallow — the NA console is small and the tunnel is close behind it | This is the number that decides whether the build fits, and it is the one no listing tells you. Measure from the back of the aperture to the nearest obstruction before you commit to a chassis depth. |
| **Fascia** | ⚠️ search: “Mazda MX-5 NA single DIN fascia” | Often not needed: the original surround usually suits a single-DIN unit directly. |
| **Harness adapter** | ⚠️ search: “Mazda to ISO 10487 harness adapter” | ⚠️ Eunos Roadster imports may carry the JDM harness rather than the European one. Check which connector is actually behind your dash rather than ordering by model year. |
| **Aerial adapter** | ⚠️ search: “Mazda aerial adapter to DIN (Motorola)” | Many NAs have a powered mast aerial — see the gotchas. |
| **Steering-wheel controls** | ⚠️ none — no factory steering-wheel audio controls | None known on any NA trim. Skip the interface box and the learning step. |
| **Dash dimmer** | ⚠️ dash dimmer at the ISO A connector | Standard ISO A6. Meter it. |
| **Switched live** | ⚠️ switched live at the ISO A connector | Standard ISO A7, commonly swapped with A4. Meter before connecting. |

**Same as the other generations**

- ISO 7736 aperture and an ISO 10487 harness via an adapter, like every car here
- No factory steering-wheel audio controls on NA or NB, so no interface box

**By market**

- UK / EU / US / AU / JP share the single-DIN aperture; the harness connector is the thing most likely to differ on a Japanese import.
- ⚠️ The radio band plan follows where the car is driven, not where it was built. An import wants the plan of the country it is in now.

**Gotchas**

- A powered mast aerial is common on the NA and it will not rise on its own. The deck has no aerial-power output. If the car has a powered or amplified aerial it needs 12 V from a switched source of your own.
- The deck is line-out only and has no amplifier. Plan for one, or accept that it will be quiet.
- It is a convertible with a thirty-year-old hood. Water in the centre console is a known NA trait, not a hypothetical one — think about where the boards sit.
- Depth. The NA console is the smallest in this directory; measure before building.

## Mazda MX-5 NC

**2005–2015** · also known as Miata NC (US), MX-5 RC / PRHT (folding hard top) · markets: UK, EU, US, JP, AU

<sub>`vehicles/mazda/mx-5/nc.json`</sub>

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| **Does the deck fit** | ⚠️ yes, but the aperture is bigger than the deck | The NC dash is believed to take a double-DIN unit. A single-DIN deck fits with a double-DIN cage and a half-height pocket or blanking plate — the standard way any 1-DIN radio goes into a 2-DIN hole. |
| **Aperture** | ⚠️ double DIN (2 × ISO 7736) | Confirm on your car. If it is double-DIN you need the pocket; if single, you do not. |
| **Depth behind the dash** | 📏 more generous than the NA/NB | This is the number that decides whether the build fits, and it is the one no listing tells you. Measure from the back of the aperture to the nearest obstruction before you commit to a chassis depth. |
| **Fascia** | ⚠️ search: “Mazda MX-5 NC double DIN fascia with 1-DIN pocket” | The pocket is the part that makes a 1-DIN deck look deliberate in a 2-DIN hole rather than lost in it. |
| **Harness adapter** | ⚠️ search: “Mazda to ISO 10487 harness adapter” | ⚠️ Cars with the Bose system are wired differently from the base system. Establish which you have before ordering. |
| **Aerial adapter** | ⚠️ search: “Mazda aerial adapter to DIN (Motorola)” | The NC generally uses a fixed aerial rather than a powered mast. |
| **Steering-wheel controls** | ⚠️ present on some trims — unlike the NA and NB | This is the one car in this directory where the steering-wheel controls are worth checking for. If yours has them, they work through the same universal interface box and the deck's learning wizard; see docs/CONTROL.md. If not, skip it. |
| **Dash dimmer** | ⚠️ dash dimmer at the ISO A connector | Standard ISO A6. |
| **Switched live** | ⚠️ switched live at the ISO A connector | Standard ISO A7. Meter it. |

**Same as the other generations**

- ISO 7736 and ISO 10487 via an adapter, as everywhere else
- ⚠️ NOT the same on steering-wheel controls: the NC may have them and the NA/NB do not

**By market**

- Trim level matters more than market on the NC, because of the Bose option and the steering-wheel controls.
- ⚠️ The radio band plan follows where the car is driven, not where it was built. An import wants the plan of the country it is in now.

**Gotchas**

- The Bose system is an amplified system and does not behave like plain speakers on an ISO block. Establish what you have before cutting anything.
- The deck is line-out only and has no amplifier. Plan for one, or accept that it will be quiet.
- The deck has no aerial-power output. If the car has a powered or amplified aerial it needs 12 V from a switched source of your own.
- A 1-DIN deck in a 2-DIN hole needs the pocket to look intentional.

## Mazda MX-5 ND

**2015–** · also known as Miata ND (US), ND2 / ND3 facelifts · markets: UK, EU, US, JP, AU

<sub>`vehicles/mazda/mx-5/nd.json`</sub>

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| **Does the deck fit** | ⚠️ no — not as a head unit | The ND has an integrated infotainment system (MZD Connect) on a screen that is part of the dash design, not a DIN slot. There is no 182 × 53 mm aperture to put this in, and the car's audio, reversing camera and vehicle settings live in the same unit. |
| **Aperture** | ⚠️ none — integrated infotainment, no DIN slot | This is a design fact about the car, not a missing adapter. |
| **Depth behind the dash** | ⚠️ not applicable | There is no aperture to measure. |
| **Fascia** | ⚠️ not applicable | Nothing to adapt to. |
| **Harness adapter** | ⚠️ not applicable as a head-unit replacement | Removing MZD Connect takes vehicle settings and the reversing camera with it. That is a different and much larger project. |
| **Aerial adapter** | ⚠️ not applicable |  |
| **Steering-wheel controls** | ⚠️ present | The ND has steering-wheel controls, which is moot while the deck cannot be the head unit. |
| **Dash dimmer** | ⚠️ not applicable |  |
| **Switched live** | ⚠️ not applicable |  |

**Same as the other generations**

- Nothing. The ND is the break in the MX-5 line for this project: NA, NB and NC take a DIN head unit and the ND does not.

**By market**

- The same everywhere — this is a limitation of the car, not of a market.
- If you want the deck in an ND, the honest answer is that it becomes a second display fed over Bluetooth or aux, not a replacement head unit. That works and it is not what the rest of this repository describes.

**Gotchas**

- ⚠️ Do not buy parts for this on the assumption an adapter exists. It is not an adapter problem.
- The deck still runs perfectly well on a desk, and the PC deck needs no car at all.

- The deck has no aerial-power output. If the car has a powered or amplified aerial it needs 12 V from a switched source of your own.
- The deck is line-out only and has no amplifier. Plan for one, or accept that it will be quiet.
- Depth unknown. Measure.

---

## Adding a car

Copy the nearest file in `vehicles/`, change what differs, run `python3 tools/vehicles/build.py`, and open a pull request. If a field does not apply — many cars have no steering-wheel controls at all — say so explicitly rather than leaving it out. "None fitted" is information; a missing key is not.

`tools/verify/test_vehicles.py` checks that every file has every field and that no claim is left without a confidence marker.
